title: Two HD 93683 fits require a minimum centre-of-mass acceleration under stated Newtonian bounds
abstract: We derive an exact Newtonian inequality between a finite change in a binary orbital plane and the acceleration of its centre of mass due to a third body. The result bounds the time integral of acceleration to the power 3/2 and its maximum. It needs bounds on inner separation, specific angular momentum and the ratio of inner barycentric radius to third-body distance. It needs no outer period, eccentricity invariant or orbit averaging. For the first published HD 93683 inclination fit, inner masses of 18 and 15 solar masses, an 8-solar-mass third body, inner osculating semimajor axis within 5 percent of its adopted value, inner eccentricity at most 0.2676553, and a separation ratio at most 0.1, acceleration must reach 7.28 km/s per year during 2002-2026. Allowing a one-degree error in each endpoint normal reduces this to 5.97 km/s per year. We give a second fit and sensitivity tests. Exact forces in 200,000 random geometries and one synthetic eight-year triple integration pass the inequalities. This is a conditional method result, not a new observation or companion detection. The fitted normal and global orbit envelopes are assumptions. The maximum can lie in the past. The physical mass centre must be distinguished from the unresolved light centre and blended spectral velocities. Code, source hashes, aggregate inputs and a static figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Necessary maximum acceleration for the first fit, with a 5 percent inner size envelope. The tests vary the separation ratio, companion mass, eccentricity cap and error in fitted normals. All bounds are conditional; none is a detection.
